gen-gf-gugi-gf-fragment-mono: Gugi's lowercase climbs almost to capital height, while Fragment Mono lines up below like nails on a ruler. Loud display shapes meet strict, precise monospace order, and neither gives ground.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-geist-mono: Gugi's tall lowercase nearly touches its capitals, and its terminals are cut open so the counters flow outward. Geist Mono brings fixed-width, code-style letters with big gaps at the sides, a structured counterweight.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-genos: Distinctive is the right word for Gugi, whose stout strokes look like drawn pipe cleaner and whose lowercase runs tall. And Genos sets its glyphs close and lets thick strokes lead the eye without dominating it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-geom: Gugi cuts its terminals open so each counter flows outward, soft and bold. Geom, a sans with a lofty lowercase band, stays approachable and contemporary through paragraph after paragraph of running text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-hammersmith-one: Hammersmith One reads clean and unfussy, its rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord and its capitals barely taller than lowercase. But Gugi's tall, open-terminal heading is the loud one, so the sans-serif text just keeps going quietly.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-inder: Bold from end to end, Gugi looks traced with a single marker, its lowercase rising nearly to cap height. Gugi grabs attention, while Inder, a sans with little height difference between cases, keeps things clean and tidy.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-jaldi: Approachable best describes Jaldi, a sans-serif with brushed-on letters, barely a gap between them, and a visibly gaping c. And its raised x-height carries the text smoothly beneath Gugi, whose horizontals weigh exactly what its verticals do.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Bowls that fill the line give the body a modern read, while Gugi's heading carries the weight of drawn wire. Kdam Thmor Pro takes over beneath it, moving the page from distinctive display to modern text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-krona-one: Bent tubing up top, loose-limbed cast iron underneath. Gugi is best at announcing itself, one tube gauge throughout, while Krona One, a sans, spaces its letters loosely and carries the text.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-magra: Professional in tone, Magra is a sans whose lowercase words all feel big-bodied, sitting under Gugi's drawn-wire heading. And since Magra already feels big, its size can come down a notch without losing presence.
